newsitem.title: UK: RESEARCH ALERT - Bass lowered at SocGen.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Bass lowered at SocGen.

text.p: Hotels-to-brewing group Bass Plc was cut to "reduce" from "hold" at SocGen, analyst Nick Lyell at the brokerage said on Friday.

Lyell said the stock was looking a little expensive on a multiple of 15.8 times expected 1997 earnings, a premium to others in the sector, especially with continuing uncertainties over its planned acquisition of Carlsberg-Tetley.

He said the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC) was due to report on the acquisition in the next few weeks but it was unlikely to be approved until after the forthcoming election, due by the end of May.
With the opposition Labour party well placed to win, the Carlsberg bid was therefore likely to be among the first to be considered by the incoming trade and industry secretary, Lyall said.

"The acquistion of Carlsberg-Tetley clearly offers great potential," Lyall said in a research note. "However, at the very least the MMC investigation provides huge uncertainties over the future structure of the group, and at worst, the bid could be blocked by a Labour government."
"Without Carlsberg-Tetley, earnigns growth would be comparable with Scottish & Newcastle Plc and would not justify the present rating."
He said the prospective change of government made it much more likely that either the takeover will be blocked or that conditions will prove harsh enough to be prohibitive.

The note added that Bass's bingo operations could be hit by the recent introduction of a midweek lottery draw, and that the U.S. hotel business appeared to be slowing, with only a very modest increase in occupancy rates expected for 1997.
Bass shares were down 6p at 858-1/2p at 1245 GMT. -- David Holmes, London Newsroom +44 171 542 5106
